verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ।
              जम्बूखण्डस्त्वया प्रोक्तो यथावदिह सञ्जय । विष्कम्भमस्य प्रब्रूहि परिमाणं तु तत्त्वतः ॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, you have described to me. Jambukhanda. Tell me now its dimensions and extent.

verses.sanskrit: समुद्रस्य प्रमाणं च सम्यगच्छिद्रदर्शनम् । शाकद्वीपं च मे ब्रूहि कुशद्वीपं च सञ्जय ॥२॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, tell me also of the extent of the oceans, of Shakadvipa, and of Kushadvipa.

verses.sanskrit: शाल्मलिं चैव तत्त्वेन क्रौञ्चद्वीपं तथैव च । ब्रूहि गावल्गणे सर्वं राहोः सोमार्कयोस्तथा ॥३॥
verses.english: Of Shalmalidvipa and of Kraunchadvipa. O son of Gavalgani, tell me also of Rahu, Soma and Surya.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच ।
              राजन्सुबहवो द्वीपा यैरिदं सन्ततं जगत् । सप्त द्वीपान्प्रवक्ष्यामि चन्द्रादित्यौ ग्रहं तथा ॥४॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O king, there are many islands in this earth. But I shall describe to you only seven islands and also the moon, and the sun and the planets.

verses.sanskrit: अष्टादश सहस्राणि योजनानि विशाम्पते । षट् शतानि च पूर्णानि विष्कम्भो जम्बुपर्वतः ॥५॥
verses.english: O king, the Jambu mountain extends for full eighteen thousand and six hundred Yojanas.

verses.sanskrit: लावणस्य समुद्रस्य विष्कम्भो द्विगुणः स्मृतः । नानाजनपदाकीर्णो मणिविद्रुमचित्रितः ॥६॥
verses.english: The extent of the salt sea is said to be double of it. this sea is covered with many kingdoms. It is adorned with gems and corals.
verses.bhavadeepa: अष्टादश सहस्त्राणि षट् शतानि च योजनानि विष्कम्भश्चतुर्दलकमलाकारस्य जम्बूद्वीपस्य पत्रान्तपरिधिः तादृशविस्तार एव पिण्डप्रमाणमन्तर्भाव्य पर्वताकृतित्वाज्जम्बूपर्वत इत्युच्यते ॥५॥

verses.sanskrit: नैकधातुविचित्रैश्च पर्वतैरुपशोभितः । सिद्धचारणसङ्कीर्णः सागरः परिमण्डलः ॥७॥
verses.english: It is adorned with many mountains that are variegated with metals of various kinds. It is circular in form like a sea, and is thickly peopled by the Siddhas and the Charanas.
verses.bhavadeepa: लावणस्येति । क्षेत्रफलतः पञ्चसहस्रायामत्वाज्जम्बूद्वीपस्य तदुभयतः पञ्चपञ्चभिः सहस्रैः समुद्रस्य विष्कम्भो विस्तारः । तेन ससमुद्रस्य द्वीपस्य पञ्चदशसहस्रयोजनो व्यासः । द्विगुणः दशसहस्रयोजनः परिमण्डलश्चेदुभयतः समुद्रवेष्टनेन सह चत्वारिंशत्सहस्रः । एवं तृतीयोऽशीतिसहस्रः । चतुर्थः षष्टिसहस्राधिकं लक्षम् । पञ्चमो लक्षत्रयं विंशतिसहस्राणि । षष्ठो लक्षषट्कं चत्वारिंशत्सहस्राणि । सप्तमो द्वादशलक्षाण्यशीतिसहस्त्राणि । एतेषां सङ्कलने पञ्चविंशतिलक्षाणि पञ्चत्रिंशत् सहस्त्राणि योजनानि सप्तानां द्वीपानां ससमुद्राणां विस्तारः ॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: शाकद्वीपं च वक्ष्यामि यथावदिह पार्थिव । शृणु मे त्वं यथान्यायं ब्रुवतः कुरुनन्दन ॥८॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata. O scion of the Kuru race, I shall now speak to you in detail of Shakadvipa. Hear as I describe it.

verses.sanskrit: जम्बूद्वीपप्रमाणेन द्विगुणः स नराधिप । विष्कम्भेण महाराज सागरोऽपि विभागशः ॥९॥
verses.english: O that island is twice as large as the Jambudvipa. O king of kings, the ocean also is twice as large as that island.

verses.sanskrit: क्षीरोदो भरतश्रेष्ठ येन सम्परिवारितः । तत्र पुण्या जनपदास्तत्र न म्रियते जनः ॥१०॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, Shakadvipa is surrounded on all sides by the sea of milk. Its kingdoms are full of righteousness and its men never die.

verses.sanskrit: कुत एव हि दुर्भिक्षं क्षमातेजोयुता हि ते । शाकद्वीपस्य सङ्क्षेपो यथावद्भरतर्षभ ॥११॥
verses.english: There is no famine there. The people all possess forgiveness and great prowess. O best of the Bharata race, I have briefly spoken to you about Shakadvipa. What else. O king, do you desire to hear.

verses.sanskrit:
उक्त एष महाराज किमन्यत्कथयामि ते ।
              धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ।
              शाकद्वीपस्य सङ्क्षेपो यथावदिह सञ्जय ॥१२॥

उक्तस्त्वया महाप्राज्ञ विस्तरं ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः ।
              सञ्जय उवाच ।
              तथैव पर्वता राजन्सप्तात्र मणिभूषिताः ॥१३॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said You have briefly told me of Shakadvipa. O greatly wise one, tell me now everything in detail.

verses.sanskrit: रत्नाकरास्तथा नद्यस्तेषां नामानि मे शृणु । अतीव गुणवत्सर्वं तत्र पुण्यं जनाधिप ॥१४॥
verses.english: O king there are seven mountains in that island. They are decked with jewels and there are mines of gems and precious stones. There are many rivers in that island. Hear, as I tell you their names. O king, every thing there is charming and delightful. The first of those mountains is called Meru. It is the abode of the celestials, the Rishis and the Gandharvas.

verses.sanskrit: देवर्षिगन्धर्वयुतः प्रथमो मेरुरुच्यते । प्रागायतो महाराज मलयो नाम पर्वतः ॥१५॥
ततो मेघाः प्रवर्तन्ते प्रभवन्ति च सर्वशः । ततः परेण कौरव्य जलधारो महागिरिः ॥१६॥
verses.english: O king, the next mountains stretching castward is called the Malaya. It is there that the clouds are born, and it is from that place that they disperse on all sides.

verses.sanskrit: ततो नित्यमुपादत्ते वासवः परमं जलम् । ततो वर्षं प्रभवति वर्षकाले जनेश्वर ॥१८॥
verses.english: O descendant of Kuru, the next is the large mountain, called Jaladhara. From it, Indra daily takes water of the best quality.
verses.bhavadeepa: रेवती ज्योतिर्मण्डलरूपेण दिवि विभ्रम्यमाणाऽपि दिव्येन रूपेणात्रापि वर्तते एवं विधिर्मर्यादा पितामहेन कृता ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit: उच्चैर्गिरी रैवतको यत्र नित्यं प्रतिष्ठिता । रेवती दिवि नक्षत्रं पितामहकृतो विधिः ॥१८॥
verses.english: O descendant of Kuru, the next is the large mountain, called Jaladhara. From it, Indra daily takes water of the best quality.
verses.bhavadeepa: रेवती ज्योतिर्मण्डलरूपेण दिवि विभ्रम्यमाणाऽपि दिव्येन रूपेणात्रापि वर्तते एवं विधिर्मर्यादा पितामहेन कृता ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit: उत्तरेण तु राजेन्द्र श्यामो नाम महागिरिः । नवमेघप्रभः प्रांशुः श्रीमानुज्ज्वलविग्रहः ॥१९॥
verses.english: O ruler of men, it is from that water that we get showers in the rains. Next is the great mountain, called Raivataka over which has been permanently placed in the sky of constellation Rohini. This arrangement has been made by the Grandsire (Brahma) himself. O great king, on the north of this mountains is one called Syama.
verses.bhavadeepa: रेवती ज्योतिर्मण्डलरूपेण दिवि विभ्रम्यमाणाऽपि दिव्येन रूपेणात्रापि वर्तते एवं विधिर्मर्यादा पितामहेन कृता ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit:
यतः श्यामत्वमापन्नाः प्रजा जनपदेश्वर ।
              धृतराष्ट्र उवाच ।
              सुमहान्संशयो मेऽद्य प्रोक्तोऽयं सञ्जय त्वया ॥२०॥
verses.english: It is as bright as the newly risen clouds. It is high beautiful and bright. O king, as the colour of that mountain is black, all the people that live there are dark.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रजाः कथं सूतपुत्र सम्प्राप्ताः श्यामतामिह ।
              सञ्जय उवाच ।
              सर्वेष्वेव महाराज द्वीपेषु कुरुनन्दन ॥२१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, a great doubt has arisen in my mind. Why, O son of Suta, people of that country are dark?

verses.sanskrit: गौरः कृष्णश्च पतगस्तयोर्वर्णान्तरे नृप । श्यामो यस्मात्प्रवृत्तो वै तस्माच्छ्यामो गिरिः स्मृतः ॥२२॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O great king, O descendant of Kuru in all islands men may be found who are fair and those who are dark and those also who are born by the mixture of the white and the black races.

verses.sanskrit: ततः परं कौरवेन्द्र दुर्गशैलो महोदयः । केसरः केसरयुतो यतो वातः प्रवर्तते ॥२३॥
verses.english: But because the people are all dark there, that mountain is called the Dark mountain. O chief of the Kurus, next to this is the great mountain, called Durgashaila.
verses.bhavadeepa: पतगवर्णं व्याचष्टे - तयोरिति । मिश्रो वर्णः पतग इत्यर्थः । ‘कारणगुणाः कार्यगुणानारभन्ते’ इति न्यायेन श्यामपर्वतभवः श्यामवर्णः शाकाद्यन्नपरिणामेन मनुष्या अपि श्यामत्वं गता इत्यर्थः । यस्मात् श्यामो गिरिस्तस्मात्तत्स्थानां श्यामो वर्णः प्रवृत्त इत्यर्थः ॥२२॥

verses.sanskrit: तेषां योजनविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्रविभागशः । वर्षाणि तेषु कौरव्य सप्तोक्तानि मनीषिभिः ॥२४॥
verses.english: Then is the mountain, called Kesari. The breezes, that blow from the mountain, are all charged with effluvia. The height of this mountain is double of the one just mentioned.

verses.sanskrit: महामेरुर्महाकाशो जलदः कुमुदोत्तरः । जलधारो महाराज सुकुमार इति स्मृतः ॥२५॥
verses.english: O descendant of Kuru it is said by the learned that there are seven Varshas in that island. The Varsha of Meru is called Mahakasha, that of the water-giver (Malaya) is called Kumudottara. That of Jaladhara is called that of Shyama, called Manikanchana.

verses.sanskrit: रेवतस्य तु कौमारः श्यामस्य मणिकाञ्चनः । केसरस्याथ मौदाकी परेण तु महापुमान् ॥२६॥
परिवार्य तु कौरव्य दैर्घ्यं ह्रस्वत्वमेव च । जम्बूद्वीपेन सङ्क्यातस्तस्य मध्ये महाद्रुमः ॥२७॥
verses.english: That of Kesara is called Modaki and that of the next mountain is called Mahapuman. In the midst of that island is a large tree called Shaka. In height and breadth that tree is equal to that of the Jambu tree in Jambudvipa. The people always worship that tree.

verses.sanskrit: शाको नाम महाराज प्रजा तस्य सदानुगा । तत्र पुण्या जनपदाः पूज्यते तत्र शङ्करः ॥२८॥
तत्र गच्छन्ति सिद्धाश्च चारणा दैवतानि च । धार्मिकाश्च प्रजा राजंश्चत्वारोऽतीव भारत ॥२९॥
verses.english: In that island there are many charming countries in which Shiva is worshipped. The Siddhas, the Charanas and the celestial go there.

verses.sanskrit: वर्णाः स्वकर्मनिरता न च स्तेनोऽत्र दृश्यते । दीर्घायुषो महाराज जरामृत्युविवर्जिताः ॥३०॥
verses.english: O king, the people there are all virtuous, O descendant of Bharata, all the four orders of men there are engaged in their respective duties. There occurs not a case of theft.

verses.sanskrit: प्रजास्तत्र विवर्धन्ते वर्षास्विव समुद्रगाः । नद्यः पुण्यजलास्तत्र गङ्गा च बहुधा गता ॥३१॥
verses.english: O king, being free from old age and death, and possessing long life, the people there grow like rivers in the rains.

verses.sanskrit: सुकुमारी कुमारी च शीताशी वेणिका तथा । महानदी च कौरव्य तथा मणिजला नदी ॥३२॥
verses.english: The rivers there are all full of sacred water. Ganga herself, distributed as she is in various countries, is also there. Sukumari, Kumari, Shitashi and Venika.

verses.sanskrit: चक्षुर्वर्धनिका चैव नदी भरतसत्तम । तत्र प्रवृत्ताः पुण्योदा नद्यः कुरुकुलोद्वह ॥३३॥
verses.english: Mahanadi, the Manijala, Chakshuas, and the river Vardhanika, O descendant of Kuru, O best of the Bharata race.

verses.sanskrit: सहस्राणां शतान्येव यतो वर्षति वासवः । न तासां नामधेयानि परिमाणं तथैव च ॥३४॥
verses.english: These and many other rivers by hundreds and thousands all full of sacred water are there. O perpetuator of the Kuru race, Vasava (Indra) draws water from them to shower as rain.

verses.sanskrit: शक्यन्ते परिसङ्ख्यातुं पुण्यास्ता हि सरिद्वराः । तत्र पुण्या जनपदाश्चत्वारो लोकसम्मताः ॥३५॥
verses.english: It is impossible to mention the names and lengths of these rivers. All of them are the foremost of all rivers, and they are all sincleansing.

verses.sanskrit: मङ्गाश्च मशकाश्चैव मानसा मन्दगास्तथा । मङ्गा ब्राह्मणभूयिष्ठाः स्वकर्मनिरता नृप ॥३६॥
verses.english: As every body has heard in the island of Shaka there are four sacred countries. They are the Mrigas, the Mashakas, the Manasas and the Mandagas.

verses.sanskrit: मशकेषु च राजन्या धार्मिकाः सर्वकामदाः । मानसाश्च महाराज वैश्यधर्मोपजीविनः ॥३७॥
verses.english: The Mrigas are generally Brahmanas engaged in the duties of their own. Many virtuous Kshatriyas are among the Mashakas who grant every wish of the Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वकामसमायुक्ताः शूरा धर्मार्थनिश्चिताः । शूद्रास्तु मन्दगा नित्यं पुरुषा धर्मशीलिनः ॥३८॥
verses.english: O king, the Manasas follow the duties of the Vaishyas. Having all their desires gratified, they are brave and firmly devoted to Dharma and Artha.

verses.sanskrit: न तत्र राजा राजेन्द्र न दण्डो न च दण्डिकाः । स्वधर्मेणैव धर्मज्ञास्ते रक्षन्ति परस्परम् ॥३९॥
verses.english: The Mandagas are all brave Shudras and they are all virtuous. O king, in these countries, there is no king, no punishment, and no person who deserves to be punished.

verses.sanskrit: एतावदेव शक्यं तु तत्र द्वीपे प्रभाषितुम् । एतदेव च श्रोतव्यं शाकद्वीपे महौजसि ॥४०॥
verses.english: They are all engaged in the practice of their respective duties and they all protect one another. So much can be said of the Shaka island and so much only could be heard of that greatly powerful isiand.
